basis: synthetic-token process CPU per replicate (F12b.6: k=0 121.04/136.38 s, k=87 189.97/208.28 s, k=145 201.80/218.57 s stress/alternative; other k interpolated); variance-x2 at the stress time; noise check projected from the 500-panel smoke (0.68 CPU-s) plus start-up; overhead measured in the F12c reduced run (9.7 and 7.2 CPU-s per invocation; 10 CPU-s budgeted) for 15 invocations

budget_barrier.code: scripts/f12_budget.py (Ledger, Meter, projection); scripts/f12_simulation.py run / noisecheck / assemble --budget-ledger --budget-plan --operator
budget_barrier.counted: parent and worker process-tree CPU of every attempt of the noise check, pilot, stage 1, coverage target, stage 2 parts, assembly, verification and other F12 simulation work, including failed and aborted attempts
budget_barrier.operator: named on the command line (--operator) and recorded in every ledger event; the chair or the session the chair assigns to the job
budget_barrier.required_for: every governed real-token run (noisecheck, pilot, stage 1, target, stage 2): the CLI refuses to start without --budget-ledger, --budget-plan and --operator
budget_barrier.rule: at launch and at every checkpoint: spent + projected remaining (planned items not completed; the running item's remaining replicates at the larger of planned and observed per-replicate CPU; overhead less overhead spent) must be <= the ceiling, else the run stops before further work, writes no report and waits for a dated prospective repricing; counts, draws and qualification work never change

ceiling_acceptance.scope: the whole F12 simulation programme: noise check, timing pilot, stage 1, coverage target, stage 2 with its 200 variance-x2 replicates, assembly / verification overhead and failed or aborted attempts; CPU on the shared machine only
ceiling_acceptance.source: docs/PREREG_H1_TF.md, A5 chair ruling on F12c (11 Nov 2026, 18:55 UTC, before any G3 outcome), accepted by Board A's F12c review (condition 7) as prospective repricing

pilot_acceptance.status: not written: the chair writes it (schema f12d-pilot-acceptance-v2, scripts/f12_simulation.py make_pilot_acceptance) only after the measured real-token timing pilot, and only if the recomputed all-in projection is within 190 CPU-h. This reconciliation backdates nothing.

pilot_projection_rule: project_cpu / all_in_projection (F12d): measured noise-check CPU + measured pilot process-tree CPU + stage 1, coverage target and stage 2 at the worst k*, + 15 x the pilot's measured per-invocation overhead. From the alternative-only pilot, stress is projected at the alternative's cost (synthetic stress / alternative ratios 0.89-0.92), every k at the k = 145 cost (synthetic cost rises with k), variance-x2 at max(stress, alternative). This is an extrapolation, labelled so; it is never measured stress timing.

stop_rules: stage 1 does not start until the chair accepts the all-in ceiling in a pilot_acceptance record (schema f12c-pilot-acceptance-v1, field all_in_ceiling_cpu_h)
after the timing pilot, project_cpu on the measured real-token CPU must project an all-in total within the accepted ceiling, else stop for a dated repricing
a projected breach during execution stops the run for a dated repricing; fixed replicate counts, draws and qualification work never change
F12d: the launch / checkpoint barrier of budget_barrier enforces these rules from the ledger; a stop never reduces counts or draws and never yields a decision from a partial run
